sentences.text:
The petitioners are seeking mandamus against the respondents to initiate acquisition proceedings in respect of Survey No. 324 measuring 6 Acres 92 Cents and Survey No.326 measuring 4 Acres,
situated at Meenkere village of Kudligi Taluk, which is utilized by the respondent-authority for formation of a Check Dam, without paying any compensation.
2.
Heard the counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents and learned HCGP.
Perused the records.
3. The reply notice issued by respondent No.5-Gram Panchayat would have a direct bearing on the petitioners' claim.

Paragraphs 1, 2 and 7 are relevant and same are culled out, which read as under:
"1. The allegations in para 1 of your legal notice that, that your client is the absolute owner and he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the land bearing Sy.No.324 and 326 measuring 4.00 acres and 6.92 acres respectively situated at Meenkere village within the jurisdiction of Kudligi Tq, Ballari district is false.

The further allegation that, the said land is derived to your client from his father and the NC:
2024:KHC-D:7324 above said two lands were granted by the government in favour of your client's father and R.K Palaiah who is the father of R.K.Basanna is false.

2. It is true that, the Panchayath Development Officer, Grama-Panchayathi,
Chirthagunda village constructed Gokatte in the above said lands, only to small extent.
It is false to allege that, it is the only the land to your client and his family member to eak-out their lively-hood 7.

It is submitted that, the villagers of Meenkere requested our client No.2 to construct a Gokatte to the stream called as 'GALERA HALLA to store water for the cattles of the village and also to in improve ground-water level.
Hence, our client No.2 sanctioned to construct Gokatte to the said stream.
The said stream is also running in the land bearing Sy No.324 extent 3.92 acres.

The joint owner R.K.Basanna, s/o R.K.Palaiah, our client No.3, approached our client No.1 & 2 and gave his consent letter on 21.2.2011 to construct Gokatte including his land, as it is required for public purpose.
At the consent and permission of the joint owner R.K.Basanna, the said Gokatte is constructed in the said land only to a small extent and completed the construction work on 18.3.2011.
Your client's father was also watching the construction work all the while and he never objected for the same.

Our Smt.G. Rukminamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85135981/
3 clients have not made any illegal construction in the said lands and they made construction with the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7324 consent of joint owner, that too for public purpose.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Your client is not entitled any reliefs, as sought in your notice."
4. On examining these three paragraphs, what can be gathered is that the respondents, having utilized the private lands, are disputing the petitioner's title over the property in question.
However at paragraph 2, respondents are admitting that portions of these private lands were utilized for construction of a Check Dam.
Paragraph 7 gives an indication that some of the owners of the above said survey numbers have consented vide letter dated 21.02.2011 for construction of Check Dam for public purpose.
One R.K.Basanna has given his consent.
It can also be gathered that the respondents have claimed that the petitioners' father was aware of the construction of Check Dam and he never objected to the construction.
Respondent No.5 asserts that the private lands are utilized after securing consent from the owners.
Whether the petitioners' father and petitioners have consented is not forthcoming from the materials.
However, a private land of poor agriculturists, who are illiterate and uneducated, cannot be utilized by securing their consent.

If petitioners' NC: 2024:KHC-D:7324 lands are utilized for public purpose, then the consequences have to follow, as it is a trite law that no citizen can be deprived of his property rights by the State and its instrumentalities without having recourse to provisions of Land Acquisition Act.

5. Though the petitioners have straight away approached this Court seeking a mandamus, the authorities shall consider this writ petition as a representation and secure records after notifying the petitioners and examine whether the petitioners' lands are utilized for the purpose of construction of Check Dam and thereafter proceed to initiate appropriate proceedings.

6. For the foregoing reasons, this Court passes the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed in part.
ii) Respondents 2 to 5 shall hold an enquiry and ascertain as to whether the petitioners' lands are utilized for the purpose of construction of Check Dam.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7324 iii) If petitioners' lands are utilized, then the Deputy Commissioner, Vijayanagar, shall take appropriate steps in accordance with law and propose to acquire petitioners' lands and pay compensation in accordance with law.
iv) This exercise shall be completed within six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Sd/-
